chunks: Ali ibn Isa al-Mujawir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us in the Mosque of Kufa, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Maqarri, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Thuwayr ibn Sa'id, from his father Sa'id ibn Aqalah, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said:

The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) ascended the pulpit of Basra and said: O people, mention my lineage. Let he who knows me mention my lineage, otherwise, I will mention my lineage by myself. I am Zaid ibn Abd-Manaf ibn Amer ibn Amr ibn Mughirah ibn Zaid ibn Kilab. Then Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up to him and said to him: O you, we do not know for you any lineage except that you are Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said to him: O you, indeed, my father named me 'Zaid' by the name of his grandfather 'Qusay', and the name of my father is 'Abd-Manaf', then the kunya (nickname) overtook the name, and indeed, the name of Abd al-Muttalib is 'Amer', then the nickname overtook the name, and the name of Hashim is 'Amr', then the nickname overtook the name, and the name of Abd-Manaf is 'Mughirah', then the nickname overtook the name, and indeed, Qusay is 'Zaid', then the Arabs named him 'Mujamma' (the Gatherer) because he gathered them from the farthest land to Mecca, then the nickname overtook the name.

key_terms.قُصَيٌّ: Qusay (ancestor of Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What are the original names of the ancestors of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) before they were known by their nicknames?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the etymology of his lineage by revealing the original personal names of his ancestors—such as Qusay, Abd-Manaf, and Hashim—which were later superseded by their more famous nicknames or kunyas. He specifically explains that 'Zaid' was his father's given name, bestowed in honor of the ancestor Qusay, whose epithet 'Mujamma' (the Gatherer) eventually became dominant. This clarification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise genealogical continuity of the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing between formal names and honorific titles to affirm their noble status within the Quraysh.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Ali bin Isa al-Mujawir, may Allah be pleased with him, in the Mosque of Kufa, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Muhammed bin Bandar, from his father, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Maqarri, from Muhammed bin Sinan, from Malik ibn ‘Atiya, from Thuwayr bin Sa’eed, from his father, Sa’eed bin ‘Ilaqa, from Hasan al-Basri, that he said:

The Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, stepped up the pulpit of Basra and said: O people, mention my lineage. Let he who knows me mention my lineage, otherwise, I will mention my lineage by myself. I am Zaid bin Abd-Manaf bin ‘Amer bin Amru bin Mughaira bin Zaid bin Kilab. Then Ibn al-Kawwa’ stood up to him and said to him: O you, we do not know for you any lineage except that you are Ali bin Abi Talib ibn Abdul-Muttalib bin Hashim bin Abd-Manaf bin Qusay bin Kilab. Then he said to him: O ignoble, indeed, my father named me Zaid, by the name of his grandfather, Qusay, and the name of my father is Abd-Manaf, then the nickname overtook the name, and indeed, the name of Abdul-Muttalib is ‘Amer, then the nickname overtook the name, and the name of Hashim is Amru, then the nickname overtook the name, and the name of Abd-Manaf is Mughaira, then the nickname overtook the name, and indeed, the name Qusayy is Zaid, then the Arabs named him jointly due to that he had gathered them from the farthest land to Mecca, then the nickname overtook the name.
